title: Arithmetic-site semantics preservation
statement: Let $x$ be a Boolean word, $B$ a natural-number register bound, $k$ an arithmetic site, $q$ a rational number, and $\sigma$ a register state. Suppose every register of $\sigma$ is at most $B$, its inner counter $b$ is at most the value of the register selected by $k$, and the value of the register selected as the scratch destination plus twice the difference between that selected comparison value and $b$ is at most $B$. If the program has probabilistic semantics $q$ from the site’s associated entry label, with the scratch destination first set to that scratch value plus twice the difference and register $3$ then set to the comparison value, then it has probabilistic semantics $q$ from the arithmetic instruction for $k$ with the original register state.
hypotheses_covered: Every register of $\sigma$ is at most $B$
The inner counter is at most the site-selected comparison register
The specified scratch update is at most $B$
Probabilistic semantics $q$ from the associated entry state with the stated register updates
replaced:
Fix an arithmetic site $k$, a rational number $q$, a register state $\sigma$, and a
bound $B$. Suppose every register of $\sigma$ is at most $B$, its inner counter is at
most the value in the site’s designated comparison register, and its designated
scratch-register value plus twice the difference between that comparison value and the
inner counter is at most $B$. If the program starting at the site’s designated entry
state with those two register updates has probabilistic semantics $q$ under the register
bound $B$, then the program starting at the corresponding arithmetic instruction with
the original register state also has probabilistic semantics $q$ under that bound.
